title: Robustness for external stores: adaptive connection pools, probabilistic load-shedding, and tiered multi-region failover
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Problem: When downstream systems (Redis, Kafka, and primary DB) degrade under bursty traffic we observe cascading latency spikes and increased error rates across the serving tier. Existing connection pools are static and global; circuit-breakers are coarse-grained. We need a pragmatic, production-safe plan to reduce blast radius while preserving critical functionality.
acceptance_criteria: Introduce adaptive connection pools with per-region and per-client limits and metrics: successful connections served per second, queue length, and avg wait time.
Implement probabilistic load-shedding for non-critical request classes (batch embedding warmups, background reranks) with configurable bleed parameters.
Deploy region-aware circuit-breakers that trip before the serving runtime SLOs are breached and trigger automatic fallback paths.

Demonstrate end-to-end behavior in staging with fault injection: under simulated Redis latency (p99+ 500ms) we keep 99th percentile API tail latency within SLOs for P99-critical routes while gracefully shedding lower-priority traffic.
Add dashboards and automated alerts that map downstream degradation to upstream error-budget consumption and recommend next actions in runbook.
tasks: Design adaptive pool algorithm (token-bucket + slow-down/backoff) and document config knobs (min_conn, max_conn, queue_limit, slow_start).
Prototype pool in runtime branch with metrics (conn_acquire_ms, conn_wait_count, conn_retries).
Implement probabilistic shedding middleware with request classification labels and dynamic thresholds driven from controller API.
Create region-aware circuit-breaker library: per-backend, per-region state, exponential backoff, and auto-recovery windows.
Write integration tests with chaos harness (inject latency/failures to Redis/Kafka/DB) and collect dashboards for validation.
Run a staged rollout: canary in eu-west-1, expand to us-west-2 after 24h burn, with automatic rollback on SLO regression.
Update runbooks and add postmortem template mapping to these new controls.
risks_mitigation: Risk: Over-aggressive shedding may drop important traffic. Mitigation: tier traffic by criticality and start with conservative shedding rates (5%).
Risk: Pool changes could introduce connection churn. Mitigation: slow-start on config changes and circuit-breaker protectors to avoid retry storms.
Risk: Multi-region failover increases egress/cost. Mitigation: autoscale regional capacity and only failover read-heavy workloads; track cost in release dashboard.
Risk: Observability gaps. Mitigation: instrument fine-grained metrics and add synthetic probes for downstream latency/availability.
